title: Stream the vowels and the parts of a string

blocks.text: Text is a stream source too: `String.chars()` gives an `IntStream` of the string's `char` values, and `Pattern.splitAsStream(text)` streams the pieces between the matches of a pattern.

items: `countVowels(String text)` returns how many characters of `text` are vowels (`a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u`, in either case); `chars()` streams the characters.

`parts(String text, String delimiter)` splits `text` at every occurrence of `delimiter` and returns the pieces trimmed, in order, leaving out empty ones. The delimiter is **plain text**, not a regular expression.

blocks.text: `String.split` takes a regular expression, and some delimiters mean something there. `Pattern.quote` turns text into a pattern that matches it literally.

cases.says: It counts the vowels of a text and splits it into trimmed parts.
Capital vowels count as vowels too.
The delimiter is plain text, so "." or "|" splits on that character, not as a regular expression.
Empty parts, from two delimiters in a row or an empty text, are left out.

concepts: A stream made from text treats its delimiter as plain text and keeps no empty parts.
